A1.title: Rain in Manchester, wind in Baku

lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about the weather.
Sam, what's the weather like in Manchester?
It's raining. Always! Sometimes snow, but no sun. I have three umbrellas.
Three? Why?
One for the house, one for the office, and one for... the other rain.
[laugh] In Baku, it's sunny today. And windy. The wind is very strong.
I know! Yesterday I went out, and the wind took my hat.
Was it hot or cold?
Cold. So I put on my coat. Then I took off my coat, because it was hot.
In one day?
In one hour! Baku has four seasons, four weathers, in one afternoon.
[laugh] It's sunny today. Do not forget your umbrella. See you next time!

words.en: sun, rain, wind and so on
the big light in the sky
soft white ice falling from the sky
you hold it over you in the rain

A2.title: Rain in Manchester, wind in Baku

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is the weather and the seasons.
Sam says the weather in Manchester is terrible. Is that true?
It's true. The forecast always says, "Cloudy with a chance of rain." And then it rains.
In summer?
In summer, too. Last July the temperature was fifteen degrees. We call that a heatwave.
[laugh] In Baku, July is thirty-five degrees. At the end of autumn it's pouring, and in winter there's a storm.
Seriously? I thought you had sun all year.
No. We have four seasons. In winter it's windy, and the north wind is freezing. We say, "It's freezing!" and then we drink tea.
What a lovely idea. When the sun comes out, we all go to the park.
And when the temperature goes down in the evening, we sit outside and talk.
In Manchester, when the temperature goes up, we take a photo and post it. Because it's rare.
"What a lovely day!" you will say. Then it rains.
Exactly. See you next time!

words.en: how hot or cold it is
very bad weather with strong wind

B1.title: Rain in Manchester, wind in Baku

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is weather — the favourite topic of British people.
Is it true that you talk about it all the time?
It is. Two Brits meet and say, "Lovely weather," or, "Terrible weather." It's not about weather, it's about being polite.
In Baku, we talk about humid summers and the heatwave in August. In June the temperature goes up and nobody works.
When I came to Baku the first time, there was a thunderstorm and a drizzle at the same time. I had no idea what to wear.
You put on a big coat, and it was thirty degrees.
Yes. People looked at me like I was a polar bear.
And in England it's raining cats and dogs one day, and the next day you're under the weather.
That's called climate. In reality, the weather is mild, damp and grey. But we go out come rain or shine.
Climate change makes it unpredictable. Some days it pours down, and then there's a flood.
Yes. A question for our listeners: what is the weather like in your city today, and how does it change your mood?
Mine: sunshine makes me happy, and rain makes me eat soup. See you next time!

words.en: the usual weather of a place
a lot of water where it should be dry
not too hot and not too cold
how hot or cold it is
